purpose: Keep console-worker retirement from renewing its wait budget between Job drain and exact process-exit observation.

baseline.path: ConsoleWorker.tryRetire created the Job drain deadline after termination, then passed the full original waitMilliseconds to the process wait after Job polling and handle close. Close supplies 5000ms and login-worker cleanup supplies 1000ms; the second phase could renew the supplied budget.
baseline.reproduction: FAIL: deterministic synctest callbacks consumed 30ms polling a Job with a 50ms budget, then received another 50ms process wait, totaling 80ms. A 70ms native Job close received another 50ms, totaling 120ms; an ordinary 15ms Job close plus process wait totaled 65ms.

change.deadline: Create one deadline before native retirement operations. Reuse it for Job polling and pass only max(0, time.Until(deadline)) rounded down to milliseconds to WaitForSingleObject. An exhausted budget still permits a nonblocking observation of exact exit.
change.ownership: WAIT_TIMEOUT still retains the exact process handle, image pin and pending retirement; it cannot publish Done or authorize another launch. Missing native-child receipts and failed handle operations retain their existing fail-closed behavior. A later zero-budget reap can observe exact exit and close resources once.
change.complexity: O(1) deadline arithmetic added; Job polling and native handle-operation counts retain their existing structure. No new timers, goroutines or I/O paths.
change.interfaces: No API, wire schema, DB, source-of-truth document, repository hygiene, runner, dependency or version changes.

validation.environment: Go 1.27.3 windows/amd64 with repository runtime STW overlay; deterministic consoleCloseOps callbacks and synctest virtual time.
validation.before: go test -timeout 2m ./internal/inputworker -run '^TestConsoleRetirementSharesOneWaitBudget$' -count=1 failed in the first three cases before the implementation change.
validation.after: PASS: the same regression, 0.042s. All four cases also verify retained process ownership after timeout and exactly-once successful retirement after a later nonblocking exact-exit observation.
validation.packages: PASS: go test -timeout 3m ./internal/inputworker ./internal/crashguard; 27.053s and 2.886s. This includes existing native Windows process/Job retirement and recovery-receipt checks.
validation.formatAndCheck: PASS: gofmt on changed Go files and git diff --check.
validation.skipped: Full repository, GUI/installer/release builds and physical two-PC tests: only console-worker retirement wait accounting changed. Installed services and applications were not updated.

remainingRisk: This accounts for elapsed native-call time but cannot preempt a native call itself or bound mutex admission. The 70ms Job-close case intentionally exceeds its 50ms budget and receives no additional process wait. Measurements use injected callbacks, not observed laptop shutdown timings, and do not establish a fix for historical input-service error 1066.
